name: Pulle Dominoes
description: Pulle is a four-player block domino game from Austria using a double-8 set of 36 tiles (doubles removed). Players contribute an equal stake to the pool (Pulle). Each round, unplayed pip counts are added to running scores; players exceeding 100 are eliminated. Last survivor wins the pool. Buy-back and broken-pool rules apply.
deck: Double-8 domino set of 36 tiles (nine doubles removed).

history.origins: Austrian domino variant; described in Domino in vielen Spielarten (Fritz Beck, Vienna, 1960). Traditionally played for money.
timeline: 1960: Described in Domino in vielen Spielarten (Fritz Beck, Vienna).
history.cultural: Played in Austria; often played for stakes; buy-back (zurückkaufen) and broken pool (gesprengte Pulle) are standard.
history.evolution: Block game variant of Austrian line dominoes; pool (Pulle) and elimination at 101+ define the game.

setup.players: Four players play as individuals. Each receives seven tiles from a 36-tile set (double-8 with nine doubles removed). No boneyard is used; it is a block game.
setup.deck: Double-8 set with nine doubles removed (36 tiles).
setup.dealing: Each player receives 7 tiles. No boneyard is used (block game). First round: holder of heaviest tile leads; thereafter the winner of the previous round leads.
setup.equipment: Double-8 domino set; optional stakes for the pool.

rules.objective: Be the last player with a running score of 100 or less; players are eliminated at 101 or more. The last survivor collects the pool (Pulle).
rules.gameplay: Block game: play a tile matching an open end of the layout or pass if unable. Tableau is built in a double line (matching end on the side). After each round, add pip total of unplayed tiles to each player's running score. At 101+ a player is eliminated unless they buy back (pay half stake, score set to middle of the other three). If all have 101+ (broken pool), scores reset to zero and everyone stakes again.
keyRules: Four players, 7 tiles each; no boneyard.
Pip total of unplayed tiles added to running score each round.
Elimination at 101 or more; 100 is still in.
Buy-back: pay half stake to pool, score becomes middle of other three.
Broken pool: everyone 101+; scores reset, everyone stakes again.

strategy.basic: Try to play out tiles early to avoid accumulating pip count; when blocked, passing is mandatory.
strategy.intermediate: Track which ends are open and which tiles opponents might hold; manage running score to stay under 100.
strategy.advanced: Use buy-back strategically when score nears 100; in broken-pool situations, consider stake size versus position.
tips: First round lead goes to holder of heaviest tile; round winner leads next.

variations.name: Per-game payment
variations.description: Winner of each round receives an amount from each opponent (e.g. 1.00 each); blocked-game winner receives half (e.g. 0.50 each). Tied blocked game: no payment, pip totals not added to running scores.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Per-game payment variant; overrides would apply if engine supported per-round payments.

scoring.description: After each round, pip total of unplayed tiles is added to running score. Players at 101 or more are eliminated. Last player with score 100 or less wins the pool.
scoring.winCondition: Last survivor with running score 100 or less wins the pool; players are eliminated at 101 or more.

synthesis.shortDescription: Four-player block domino with pool stakes; elimination at 101+; buy-back and broken-pool rules.
